rationale: Objective is max-rank NCCL kernel-duration sum, and the project contract states those durations include device waiting, not wire time. The frozen step issues exactly 13 cross-rank-matched allreduces through the one editable dispatch boundary c10d.allreduce_.default: 12 buckets of 7,087,872 fp32 elements (28,351,488 B; call d0938de87369efd500322679) plus the is-last embedding bucket of 39,385,344 elements (157,541,376 B; call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b), both parented by project.invoke 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0. Measured decomposition: collective_calibration at the exact observed sizes gives a pure-transfer floor of ~3.58 ms per 28.35 MB bucket and ~19.48 ms for the 157.5 MB bucket (~7.9-8.1 GB/s over SHM, peer access disabled, ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL), i.e. ~62.4-63.6 ms for all 13 collectives per rank; the flat per-byte rate across the 5.6x size range rules out re-bucketing/coalescing gains, and payload identity bars payload reduction. Clean baseline: rank 0 at 62.08-63.14 ms (equal to the floor; it waits for nobody) while rank 1, which sets the 86.48 ms objective, carries ~21-24 ms of pure waiting on the identical floor. Where the wait lives is directly observed: execution_timeline shows a ~15 ms per-collective CPU-submission offset in the instrumented capture (rank 0 submitting early, its seq-21 kernel stretched to 18.5 ms vs 3.6 ms pure) and a ~2.6-2.8 ms per-bucket submit cadence on both ranks; nsys shows the same shape (early rank's first kernel absorbing the wait, remaining kernels at pure durations); in every collection context the max-rank sum equals transfer floor plus inter-rank submit/arrival skew absorbed inside the NCCL kernels of whichever rank arrives first (rank 1 in clean runs, rank 0 under instrumentation). Change made here: each replacement first performs a CPU-side gloo rendezvous (dist.barrier on the adapter's existing out-of-band gloo control group from state, created in prepare outside timing; a dedicated gloo group is lazily created once per process only in the unexpected case that control is absent) and only then issues the original allreduce unchanged through context.references with identical tensors, process group 0, ReduceOp.SUM and async semantics. Both ranks therefore submit each of the 13 collectives within the rendezvous residual (~sub-ms) instead of the observed ~15-24 ms offset. Because an NCCL kernel duration is transfer plus spin-wait for the peer, the migrated wait moves from the GPU kernels (counted by communication_kernel_sum_ms) to CPU barrier time (a gloo barrier launches no NCCL/CUDA kernel and adds nothing to the objective), while the reduction stays bit-identical: same op, same operands, same communicator. The wait itself was already on the critical path as GPU spin on the early rank and as arrival delay on the late rank, so step_ms changes only by the 13 CPU rendezvous round trips (~0.1-0.3 ms each expected) against the 7.1 ms budget of the 1.05x constraint (141.3 ms baseline); the workload still executes fully on every invocation, no outputs are cached, and all 13 parent allreduces still execute through the references, so gradients, parameters, loss, collective identity and logical payload are untouched. Joint scope is required because the mechanism must cover the whole 13-call sequence at this dispatch target: synchronizing only one group would leave the remaining dispatches staggered and the first-kernel wait pattern intact. Expected effect to be tested: diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms falls from 86.48 ms toward the measured pure-transfer floor, roughly 63-68 ms (-21% to -27%), with step_ms within 1.05x. There is no inputs/previous-feedback.txt or previous-candidate for this task, so this is the first attempt and no prior failure needs revision. The rendezvous_stride parameter exists only as a legal tuning dial for the barrier cadence (rendezvous every k-th guarded allreduce in program order, 1 = every call) in case the CPU round trips bind the step_ms constraint; every choice leaves the allreduce operands, process group, op and async semantics unchanged, and guard outcomes are decided by rank-symmetric argument values so both ranks make identical rendezvous decisions. Known unknowns that could bound the benefit: residual submit jitter and GPU-readiness (launch-to-kernel-start) skew after the rendezvous set the achievable floor; clean-run diagnostics cannot directly resolve whether part of the ~24 ms is one-time first-kernel absorption rather than per-collective stagger (instrumented evidence shows per-collective stagger, and per-call rendezvous covers re-accumulation); and the gloo barriers are new out-of-band CPU collectives inside the run boundary which must be verified not to disturb the framework's cross-rank collective matching.

setup_work.build_time: No parameter transforms, no CUDA allocations, no CUDA Graph capture, no module wrappers. build(context) reads the gloo rendezvous group handle from state['control'] (the adapter's existing out-of-band control group created in prepare, outside timing) and derives the expected per-site bucket sizes from context['targets']. Nothing GPU-facing happens at installation; no parent call is made at build time.
setup_work.runtime_setup: If state['control'] is absent (not the case for this adapter), a dedicated gloo group is lazily created exactly once per process at the first guarded allreduce, guarded by a module-level lock; with warmup=2 preceding measured repeats this one-time store rendezvous is absorbed outside measured samples. With control present, no setup lands inside any measured step.
setup_work.persistent_state: A monotonic event counter (for the rendezvous_stride cadence) and a cached group handle persist across invocations; both are order-based process state, not caches of fixture-dependent outputs, so reset(), continuous execution and repeated invocations are unaffected. The gloo barrier itself uses small transient CPU tensors only.
setup_work.memory_report: No new CUDA allocations: framework.peak_allocated_bytes, framework.peak_reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peaks are expected unchanged; the rendezvous adds no NCCL/CUDA kernel and no GPU memory. No physical-memory saving is claimed.
setup_work.synchronization: dist.barrier(group=<gloo control group>, async_op=False) executes on the CPU before each guarded allreduce submission; the parent NCCL allreduce is then called with unmodified args/kwargs, preserving stream, async Work semantics and gradient_as_bucket_view aliasing. Barrier ordering is safe because both ranks execute the identical 13-event sequence per run (guard decisions depend only on rank-symmetric argument values) and the adapter's before_run barrier on the same group stays order-consistent across the run cycle; an asymmetric crash would surface as a bounded 120 s gloo timeout, not an unbounded hang.

quality_risks: The 13 per-collective gloo barriers are new out-of-band CPU collectives inside the run boundary (on the adapter's control group, carrying no payload, mirroring the source's own control-group usage which normally sits outside timing). If the framework's collective_identity/cross_rank_collectives validation rejects any run-boundary collective beyond the 13 payload-identical NCCL allreduces on group 0, this attempt fails and a store-based non-collective rendezvous would be the follow-up design; the required observations should otherwise still see 13 payload-identical, cross-rank-matched allreduces with unchanged collective identity.

step_ms budget: 13 CPU rendezvous round trips land on the late rank's critical path (~0.1-0.3 ms each expected over local transport, ~1.3-4 ms total) against the 7.1 ms headroom of the 1.05x constraint; if gloo latency per barrier is worse than expected the constraint could bind, which the rendezvous_stride parameter (2 or 3) mitigates at the cost of residual skew on skipped collectives.

The achievable objective floor is bounded by residual submit jitter and GPU-readiness (launch-to-kernel-start) skew that a CPU rendezvous cannot remove; expected landing is ~62-68 ms, not below the measured pure-transfer floor of ~62.4 ms, and no claim is made that the floor itself improves.

Clean-run skew attribution: instrumented evidence shows per-collective stagger, but clean diagnostics cannot rule out that part of the ~24 ms rank-1 excess is one-time first-kernel absorption; if so the realized gain is smaller than projected, though per-call rendezvous still bounds re-accumulation. The skew direction flips between contexts (rank 1 in clean runs, rank 0 under instrumentation); the mechanism is symmetric and direction-agnostic.

Numerics: the parent allreduce is invoked with identical tensors, process group, ReduceOp and async semantics, so loss, gradients and parameter updates are expected bit-identical (grad/parameter tolerances 1e-6/1e-4); the only semantic addition is CPU-side blocking before submission, which does not alter autograd results or bucket views.

Route labels are diagnostic self-report only; acceptance relies on the framework's runtime coverage of the two replacement sites and its independent observation of the 13 parent calls through context.references, all of which still execute (eliminated_calls is empty).

params.name: rendezvous_stride
params.description: Perform the CPU gloo rendezvous every k-th guarded allreduce in program order across both call sites (1 = before every collective, the projected optimum). Choices 2 and 3 trade residual inter-rank skew on skipped collectives for fewer barrier round trips if step_ms overhead binds. The allreduce operands, process group, ReduceOp, async semantics and all workload/quality thresholds are identical for every choice; stride only gates whether a barrier precedes a given submission, and the event counter advances identically on all ranks.
